topic: Universal heteroskedastic dominance of late batched arm elimination: for every K>=3 and every finite positive known Gaussian variance vector, compare a fully specified proportional two-batch eliminate-one design with the variance-aware static allocation maximizing the worst equal-gap pair exponent; prove strict instancewise error-exponent improvement for every unique-best mean vector, compute C_h by one-dimensional piecewise-quadratic projections, eta=min_i w_i/(1-w_i), rho=(1+eta)/(C+eta), and gain G=C(1+eta)/(C+eta)>1, establish the exact finite-branch Gaussian exponent and matching elimination/terminal witnesses within the proportional family, and supply a conservative finite-T Chernoff certificate for successive-elimination software and heteroskedastic multi-arm fundraising experiments. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Presolve analytically derived C_h=min_{t>=0}[t^2/(2v_h)+sum_{j!=h}(sqrt(2(v_h+v_j))-t)_+^2/(2v_j)]>1, the lower-bound multiplier G, and whole-positive-orthant dominance; equal-variance, severe-imbalance, near-tie, K=2, and (1,1,4) regimes were checked, with the latter giving G approximately 1.044815499855. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently prove finite-branch Gaussian LDP equality and terminal-branch attainment showing G is the exact optimal worst-instance multiplier within the proportional two-batch family, including branch coupling and rounding. EARLY KILL TEST: Recompute the K=3 variance (1,1,4) best-elimination and terminal-comparison witnesses in exact algebraic arithmetic; stop if either contradicts the projection or coupling formula. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_heterovar_bae_dominance_frontier.md

open_problems.open_problem: Does a fully specified proportional two-batch eliminate-one design have an exact finite-branch Gaussian large-deviation exponent equal to the minimum of its best-arm-elimination and terminal-misranking quadratic programs for every positive known variance vector and every unique-best treatment-mean vector?

source_refs.claim: Adaptive fixed-budget sampling is harder than static sampling; the paper connects large deviations of random sampling proportions to those of empirical rewards.
source_refs.author: Po-An Wang, Ruo-Chun Tzeng, Alexandre Proutiere

source_refs.claim: SHVar gives exponential error upper bounds under known heterogeneous variances but not an exact branchwise exponent with matching witnesses.
source_refs.author: Anusha Lalitha, Kousha Kalantari, Yifei Ma, Anoop Deoras, Branislav Kveton

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing heterogeneous-variance elimination analysis uses concentration and deterministic pull-count bounds, while adaptive-LDP analysis requires control of random sampling proportions. In the two-batch rule, the first-batch Gaussian ordering simultaneously selects the eliminated arm and changes all second-batch sample sizes, coupling the terminal comparison to the selection branch. A proof must handle joint contractions, boundaries where branches meet, reuse of first-batch observations, and integer rounding; an upper-bound union argument alone cannot establish equality or terminal-branch attainment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equality theorem expressing the error exponent as a finite minimum of explicit Gaussian quadratic programs over elimination and terminal branches, with an attaining deviation witness for every active branch and a proof that floor and ceiling allocation changes are exponentially negligible.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing makes heterogeneous treatment variances the operational reason to alter fixed-budget allocation and separates known-variance from unknown-variance designs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fixed experimental budget with heterogeneous treatment noise -> equal allocation wastes observations on precise arms -> variance-aware elimination reallocates observations -> its exact branchwise error exponent remains unknown

method_exemplars.technique: Establish a large-deviation principle for empirical sampling proportions and rewards, then contract the joint rate function onto the misidentification event.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired exponent is a contraction for an adaptive allocation whose second-stage proportions are selected by first-stage empirical rewards.

method_exemplars.technique: Use bandit change-of-measure inequalities and exact Gaussian two-arm allocations to construct matching exponent lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each proposed terminal or elimination witness locally reduces to Gaussian alternatives exchanging the identity of the best treatment.

open_problems.open_problem: For every K at least three and every finite positive known Gaussian variance vector, does proportional late eliminate-one sampling strictly improve the instancewise error exponent over the variance-only static allocation maximizing the worst equal-gap exponent, or is there a unique-best counterexample?

source_refs.claim: Generalized Neyman allocation is worst-case optimal for heteroskedastic Gaussian arms in an equal-gap local regime, without establishing pointwise optimality away from that regime.
source_refs.author: Masahiro Kato

source_refs.claim: For K at least three, no algorithm uniformly matches the stronger mean-aware static-oracle exponent over all instances in a one-parameter natural exponential family.
source_refs.author: Motti Goldberger

source_refs.claim: Instance-dependent fixed-budget error exponents and uniformly competitive procedures are identified as central unresolved questions.
source_refs.author: Chao Qin

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kato's variance-aware allocation is calibrated to a minimax equal-gap experiment rather than every mean vector, while Goldberger excludes universal matching of the stronger mean-aware static oracle. Strict dominance over the weaker variance-only benchmark is therefore neither implied nor contradicted. The obstacle is a uniform comparison of two nonsmooth minima over challenger pairs and coupled elimination or terminal branches across active-pair changes and extreme variance imbalance. Any proposed positive-orthant proof must first reproduce the K=3 variance vector (1,1,4) elimination and terminal witnesses in exact arithmetic; a contradiction there would furnish an early counterexample to the claimed projection or coupling formula.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform strict inequality between the two explicit exponent functions on every unique-best mean cone, with equality characterized on its boundary, or an exact positive-variance unique-best counterexample specifying the active static pair and active elimination or terminal branch.

writing_exemplar.why: It organizes fixed-budget best-arm identification around the precise question of which exponent can be achieved uniformly over instances.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fixed-budget treatment choice lacks a settled instancewise complexity -> the static benchmark is explicit but mean-dependent -> uniform matching of that oracle fails -> test late adaptation against the weaker variance-only maximin benchmark

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize Gaussian misidentification exponents under generalized Neyman allocation and derive matching local equal-gap lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the heteroskedastic static comparator and identifies the equal-gap configurations for which that comparator is calibrated.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply change of measure to translated hard-instance families to bound every algorithm's exponent relative to the static oracle.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its benchmark separation prevents a result about the variance-only comparator from being overstated as impossible uniform domination of the mean-aware oracle.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact optimal worst-instance exponent multiplier over the variance-aware static equal-gap benchmark within the full class of proportional two-batch eliminate-one Gaussian treatment-allocation designs, and do elimination and terminal branches both attain it for every variance profile?

source_refs.claim: Adaptive large deviations sharpen elimination-algorithm guarantees but do not optimize the exact worst-instance multiplier within a proportional two-batch subclass.
source_refs.author: Po-An Wang, Ruo-Chun Tzeng, Alexandre Proutiere

source_refs.claim: Batch-constrained top-arm identification is studied under fixed-budget and fixed-confidence criteria without an exact heteroskedastic two-batch minimax schedule.
source_refs.author: Kwang-Sung Jun, Kevin Jamieson, Robert Nowak, Xiaojin Zhu

source_refs.claim: Three batches suffice for asymptotically optimal fixed-confidence sample complexity, which does not settle exact fixed-budget exponents under a two-batch constraint.
source_refs.author: Tianyuan Jin, Yu Yang, Jing Tang, Xiaokui Xiao, Pan Xu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Batched results chiefly optimize sample and batch complexity in fixed confidence, while fixed-budget work generally provides exponent bounds rather than an exact constrained-class game. The missing reduction is from the continuum of unique-best instances to finitely many least-favorable branches: one must exclude worse unequal-gap or coupled terminal configurations and then optimize the first-batch fraction against elimination and terminal witness families simultaneously.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax theorem evaluating the supremum over proportional two-batch parameters and infimum over unique-best Gaussian mean vectors as a closed-form one-dimensional piecewise-quadratic value, with explicit least-favorable elimination and terminal witnesses and a complete characterization of optimal schedules.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates exact error-exponent analysis by contrasting explicit static large deviations with the difficulty created by adaptive sampling.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Static Gaussian exponents are explicit -> adaptive elimination makes allocation data-dependent -> available guarantees leave constrained designs unoptimized -> solve the exact proportional two-batch minimax game

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer a sampling-proportion LDP to empirical rewards and reduce misidentification to variational rate functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired multiplier is an infimum of branchwise variational rates over treatment-mean instances.

method_exemplars.technique: Formulate fixed-budget minimax rates as an optimization over instances and sampling rules and construct a rule attaining the resulting rate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a structurally analogous max-min exponent game, while the destination imposes the sharper proportional two-batch constraint.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the asymptotic heteroskedastic two-batch exponent be converted into a conservative finite-T Chernoff certificate for selecting the best fundraising treatment, with explicit branch prefactors and exact losses from proportional integer rounding?

source_refs.claim: SHVar supplies a finite-budget exponential upper bound for heterogeneous variances, but with stagewise constants rather than the exact late-elimination exponent.
source_refs.author: Anusha Lalitha, Kousha Kalantari, Yifei Ma, Anoop Deoras, Branislav Kveton

source_refs.claim: Successive Rejects provides parameter-free finite-budget exponential guarantees and is a foundational deployable elimination procedure.
source_refs.author: Jean-Yves Audibert, Sebastien Bubeck, Remi Munos

source_refs.claim: Large-deviation analysis sharpens asymptotic exponents for elimination rules but does not itself produce a rounded two-batch finite-T certificate.
source_refs.author: Po-An Wang, Ruo-Chun Tzeng, Alexandre Proutiere

open_problems.why_unsolved: A large-deviation exponent suppresses polynomial prefactors and bounded allocation perturbations, whereas software operates at an integer budget. The proof must enumerate only feasible elimination and terminal branches without sacrificing the sharp rate, while tracking floors, ceilings, minimum-pull constraints, and dependence caused by reusing first-batch observations in the final comparison. Existing heterogeneous-variance bounds do not provide the requested threshold at which a rounded adaptive design is certified to dominate its rounded static comparator.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A nonasymptotic bound of the form P(error) at most A(K,T,v) exp[-T Gamma(mu,v)+R(K,v)] with explicit computable A and R for the rounded proportional rule, plus a computable threshold T0 beyond which its certified bound is strictly smaller than the corresponding rounded static-design certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: Its presentation connects heterogeneous-variance best-arm identification to operational A/B testing and states guarantees directly in finite-budget error-probability language.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fundraising software has a fixed integer treatment budget -> heterogeneous variances demand nonuniform allocation -> an asymptotic gain does not certify a finite deployment -> derive a computable finite-T error guarantee

method_exemplars.technique: Combine deterministic pull-count bounds for variance-proportional scheduling with pairwise sub-Gaussian tails and a stagewise error decomposition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination uses the same known-variance allocation mechanics but requires sharper branch accounting and rounding constants.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian likelihood ratios and change-of-measure bounds to calibrate finite-error guarantees against asymptotic limits.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These tools can test whether the nonasymptotic certificate retains the correct pairwise Gaussian exponent.

open_problems.open_problem: If Gaussian treatment variances are unknown, can a pilot-plus-proportional eliminate-one design with K at least three retain the oracle known-variance two-batch instancewise exponent, and what pilot size is necessary and sufficient?

source_refs.claim: SHAdaVar handles unknown heterogeneous variances with optimistic estimates and a finite-budget upper bound but does not establish the known-variance oracle exponent.
source_refs.author: Anusha Lalitha, Kousha Kalantari, Yifei Ma, Anoop Deoras, Branislav Kveton

source_refs.claim: Empirical-variance and transportation-cost methods address unknown Gaussian variances in fixed confidence, leaving the fixed-budget K-arm exponent separate.
source_refs.author: Marc Jourdan, Remy Degenne, Emilie Kaufmann

source_refs.claim: A pilot, elimination, and estimated-variance second stage is studied for minimax and Bayes simple regret rather than an exact instancewise probability-of-error exponent.
source_refs.author: Masahiro Kato

open_problems.why_unsolved: Replacing known variances by estimates turns the second-stage allocation into a random function of pilot sample variances. The fixed quadratic Gaussian contraction then fails: sample means and variances must be treated jointly, and exponentially rare variance underestimation may starve an arm enough to determine the error rate. Existing fixed-confidence wrappers and simple-regret results do not determine whether a vanishing, logarithmic, or fixed-fraction pilot preserves the known-variance instancewise exponent.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient pilot-size theorem and joint mean-variance large-deviation principle proving equality with the known-variance branchwise exponent, or an explicit exponent-loss formula with a least-favorable variance-estimation witness when equality is impossible.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames a two-stage treatment-choice design around a pilot that eliminates arms and estimates variances before variance-proportional allocation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Treatment variances are unknown before experimentation -> a pilot estimates noise and removes weak treatments -> the second stage adapts to estimated variances -> determine whether the practical rule retains the known-variance oracle exponent

method_exemplars.technique: Construct empirical-variance transportation costs and prove time-uniform joint control of Gaussian sample means and variances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The method directly controls plug-in variances that determine later allocations, although its proof must be rebuilt for fixed-budget exponential rates.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish an LDP for adaptive sampling proportions and contract it jointly with empirical rewards.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Unknown-variance proportional allocation produces the random-proportion deviations that may dominate the final error exponent.

literature_map:
Qin (2022, COLT, arXiv:2303.00950) records instance-dependent fixed-budget optimality as a central open problem.
Kaufmann, Cappe, and Garivier (2016, JMLR, arXiv:1407.4443) give refined lower bounds and matching Gaussian conclusions only in restricted cases, including two arms.
Audibert, Bubeck, and Munos (2010, COLT) introduce Successive Rejects with parameter-free exponential guarantees.
Karnin, Koren, and Somekh (2013, ICML) introduce Sequential Halving and near-optimal gap-dependent guarantees.
Carpentier and Locatelli (2016, COLT, arXiv:1605.09004) prove fixed-budget lower bounds with a characteristic log-K loss for gap-complexity benchmarks.
Jun, Jamieson, Nowak, and Zhu (2016, AISTATS) study batched arm pulls without exact heteroskedastic two-batch exponents.
Komiyama, Tsuchiya, and Honda (2022, NeurIPS, arXiv:2206.04646) formulate minimax fixed-budget exponent rates and attaining procedures.
Degenne (2023, COLT, arXiv:2303.09468) shows that a universally attained fixed-budget complexity exists only under restrictive conditions tied to the nonadaptive oracle.
Lalitha, Kalantari, Ma, Deoras, and Kveton (2023, UAI, arXiv:2306.07549) give SHVar and SHAdaVar for heterogeneous known and unknown variances, with bounds rather than exact branchwise rates.
Wang, Tzeng, and Proutiere (2023, NeurIPS, arXiv:2312.12137) connect LDPs of adaptive sampling proportions and rewards and sharpen elimination exponents.
Kato (2023, arXiv:2310.19788) derives generalized Neyman allocation for heteroskedastic Gaussian arms and proves worst-case optimality in an equal-gap local regime.
Jin, Yang, Tang, Xiao, and Xu (2024, NeurIPS, arXiv:2310.14129) attain optimal fixed-confidence complexity in three batches, leaving the exact two-batch fixed-budget frontier open.
Jourdan, Degenne, and Kaufmann (2023, ALT, arXiv:2210.00974) develop empirical-variance and transportation-cost tools for unknown-variance Gaussian BAI in fixed confidence.
Xiong, Camilleri, Fazel, Jain, and Jamieson (2024, AISTATS, arXiv:2307.15154) show why nonstationary A/B/n experiments require robust allocation and a counterfactual full-horizon target.
Goldberger (2026, arXiv:2607.11635) proves that no algorithm uniformly matches the mean-aware static-oracle exponent for K at least three, so a universal dominance theorem must use a weaker benchmark.
